summary: Episode Twenty-Two is the Ex-Lover Show, although only Luna—an artist and former partner of David Choe—accepts the invitation. The opening follows Asa Akira and Yoshi Obayashi in Philadelphia, then turns toward which former partners might appear and why most would refuse. Asa describes an ex-partner whom she says fabricated family and sexual-trauma stories; the archive leaves him unidentified. A discussion of adult-film director Chico Wang includes an allegation that the episode states too definitively; editorial metadata records only that he was investigated in connection with his wife's death. Luna describes meeting David while working at Upper Playground, initially disliking his work, reconnecting through social media, seeing his improvised stand-up at the Echoplex, and later attending a group dinner at Lawry's. They reconstruct a relationship that both framed as casual but experienced as increasingly intense. Their memories diverge over who initiated sex, what was promised, when feelings appeared, who ended the relationship, and whether honesty about avoiding commitment prevents harm. David describes intimacy avoidance, deliberately choosing incompatible partners, maintaining an internal disqualification list, and treating a partner's child as a boundary. Luna says she often learned his feelings only during this recording. The episode therefore functions less as a verdict than as two people discovering that their supposedly explicit arrangement contained different information. Trivia covers middle names, Adam Sandler films, and Bill Murray. Turn segmentation was deliberately skipped; named dialogue remains withheld pending independent speaker-range validation.

connections.label: The episode's form exposes asymmetric information
connections.note: David and Luna say they discussed avoiding a relationship, yet Luna learns during the recording that he had feelings and a private list of objections. Explicit rules cannot create informed consent when relevant information stays internal.

connections.label: An ex-lover archive must preserve disagreement without arbitrating private truth
connections.note: They remember initiation, sexual firsts, promises, feelings, and the breakup differently. The useful record shows both accounts and timestamps rather than collapsing the exchange into one authoritative retrospective.

connections.label: Public candor can coexist with interpersonal avoidance
connections.note: David discusses sex and motives before an audience while describing how he evades direct attachment. Radical disclosure on a microphone does not guarantee timely disclosure to the person affected.

connections.label: The home is simultaneously trust evidence and a barrier
connections.note: David rarely lets partners know where he lives, so inviting Luna signals unusual access. The severe disorder, darkness, and lack of ordinary domestic space also make the home unsuitable for sustained shared life.

connections.label: Choosing incompatible partners is a form of controlled intimacy
connections.note: David says he selects women he is unlikely to love, maintains a disqualification list, and limits contact with a partner's child. The strategy permits intensity while preserving prewritten reasons to leave.

connections.label: A declared casual arrangement can still accumulate obligations
connections.note: Repeated sex, access to private space, food rituals, exclusivity questions, jealousy, and emotional discovery generate relationship-like consequences even when both people reject the label.

connections.label: Children make adult ambiguity materially different
connections.note: David treats meeting Luna's child as a line he should not cross casually. Whatever the adults call their arrangement, involving a child creates continuity and attachment that cannot be dismissed through terminology.

connections.label: The show corrects one allegation by changing metadata, not dialogue
connections.note: Participants state that Chico Wang murdered his partner. Available public records support that he was investigated, not convicted. The transcript stays faithful while the index and summary use the narrower evidence-backed wording.

connections.label: Fan criticism mirrors romantic criticism
connections.note: David argues that one hostile comment can overpower ten positive ones, then responds similarly to imagined comparison with better partners. In both contexts, anticipated rejection becomes evidence before the other person supplies it.

connections.label: Trivia demonstrates layered correction again
connections.note: William, Walter, Chewbacca, Wild Things, and “Mr. Fop” are live wrong guesses and must remain wrong. “Billy Murray,” “Scarlet Tokyo,” and “Lots in translation” are ASR damage. The editorial process repairs the model without improving the players' scores or supplying unspoken words.

connections.label: Fan and platform records establish provenance
connections.note: The surviving fan ledger identifies Episode 022 as the May 21, 2013 Ex-Lover Show, and Mixcloud describes David's ex-girlfriend with Asa, Zell, Yoshi, and Bobby. Those records confirm structure; the recording remains authoritative for content.

connections.label: Text and speaker confidence remain separate
connections.note: Episode Twenty-Two is a strong searchable draft with 2,196 fixed-window identity embeddings. Because turn segmentation was deliberately skipped and held-out multi-speaker validation remains incomplete, individual speaker labels stay unpublished.

Private ex-partners and children are not indexed, and unresolved allegations are not presented as adjudicated facts.
